metadata.title: Low Metallicity Indicates that the Hypervelocity Star HE 0437-5439 was Ejected from the LMC

evidence.quote: HE 0437–5439 was Ejected from the LMC
HE 0437–5439 stands out as the most enigmatic one.
We measure the chemical abundance of the hypervelocity star HE 0437–5439
Edelmann et al. (2005) discovered this HVS during a spectroscopic follow-up of their sample of subluminous B-star candidates from the Hamburg/ESO survey
Motivated by these intriguing scenarios, we set out to measure the metallicity of HE 0437–5439 and obtained photometry to search for variability.

notes: HE 0437–5439 is included as follow_up: it was already identified as an HVS by Edelmann et al. (2005) (T:p2-b2), and this paper analyzes it to measure its metallicity and search for variability (T:p2-b4). The paper's final preference for an LMC origin does not change the follow_up classification. No Gaia identifier is given in the supplied material.

HE 0437–5439: T:p2-b2 explicitly identifies 61 ± 12 kpc as a distance from the Galactic center, not a heliocentric distance. T:p5-b1 calls 73_{-5}^{+6} kpc the recalculated "distance ... following Edelmann et al. (2005)"; because Edelmann et al.'s reported quantity is Galactocentric, this is recorded as galactocentric_radius. T:p5-b1 does not explicitly restate the radial-velocity frame for the 723 ± 2 km/s confirmation. No equatorial coordinates, parallax, proper motions, total Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound probabilities are reported.
